newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Cameroon minister resigns, to run for president.
newsitem.headline: Cameroon minister resigns, to run for president.

text.p: Cameroon's Health Minister Titus Edzoa, once a close aide of President Paul Biya, said on Sunday that he was resigning his portfolio and would contest presidential elections planned for October.

Edzoa, who held the powerful post of secretary general at the presidency until a government reshuffle last September, denounced what he called "underhand acts" preventing him from accomplishing his mission as minister.

"Faced with this generally vexed situation...I have decided to...put an end, from this very moment, to my position as minister of public health," he told Gabon-based Africa Number One radio station in an interview.

"I have decided to declare my candidacy in the upcoming presidential elections. I am thus giving Cameroonians another possibility for change," he said in remarks monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.
Officials at Cameroon's presidency said they were aware that Edzoa planned to resign to challenge Biya.

Edzoa is the third one-time Biya ally who has announced plans to stand against him. The others are Ayissi Nvondo and Albert Dnzongang, both once prominent members of Biya's ruling Democratic Rally of the Cameroonian People (RDPC).
Party sources say that other RDPC stalwarts were angry at being denied the chance during party primaries to stand for parliament's 180 seats on May 17.
The opposition in a country plagued by a French-English linguistic divide has not yet made clear whether it will put up a common candidate for the presidential polls.
Biya took over from independence president Ahmadou Ahidjo in 1982. He won the 1992 presidential poll with 39.9 percent of votes cast, just ahead of Anglophone rival John Fru Ndi.
